interest: This file provides valuable insight into the post-World War II allocation of Japanese military supplies, public health shortages in transitional pre-independence India, and the legal frameworks governing Allied occupation policy. It highlights how the Far Eastern Commission's restitution policy (FEC 011/12) took legal precedence over urgent civilian medicinal needs, strictly classifying Japanese military quinine reserves as looted property subject to restitution rather than commercial export or reparations. Additionally, the correspondence illustrates bureaucratic delays and communication friction between the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP) in Tokyo, its Economic and Scientific Section (ESS), and the State Department in Washington.
keywords: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
overview: This file comprises diplomatic correspondence from January to March 1947 between the Embassy of India in Washington, D.C., and the U.S. Department of State's Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs regarding the Government of India's request to obtain stocks of quinine surrendered by or seized from the Japanese Army and Navy. After P. A. Menon of the Indian Embassy followed up on an earlier July 1946 inquiry, Associate Chief Roswell H. Whitman noted that an initial survey reported by the Economic and Scientific Section in Tokyo appeared to have been erroneous and that further inquiries were underway. Ultimately, Division Chief Edwin M. Martin notified the Indian Embassy that the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers determined the quinine stocks in Japan to be looted property, making them ineligible for export under Far Eastern Commission policy FEC 011/12 on the Restitution of Looted Property.

subfiles.about: The Embassy of India follows up on a previous request regarding the procurement of quinine surrendered by the Japanese Army and Navy.
subfiles.summary: P. A. Menon of the Embassy of India writes to Roswell Whitman at the State Department's Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs, referencing an earlier inquiry by M. R. A. Baig dated July 31, 1946. Menon emphasizes that the Government of India urgently requires quinine taken from the Japanese armed forces and requests an update on the availability and status of these stocks.
subfiles.title: Letter from P. A. Menon to Roswell Whitman regarding quinine required by India
subfiles.to: Roswell Whitman (Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs, Department of State)

subfiles.about: The Department of State informs the Indian Embassy of delays in assessing quinine availability in Tokyo and promises a follow-up inquiry.
subfiles.from: Roswell H. Whitman (Associate Chief, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs, Department of State)
subfiles.summary: Roswell H. Whitman replies to P. A. Menon regarding the availability of quinine in occupied Japan. He explains that while SCAP reported in September 1946 that a survey was being conducted, no further advice had arrived, and suggests that an initial report by the Economic and Scientific Section was likely mistaken. Whitman apologizes for the prolonged delay and assures Menon that a follow-up cable will be sent to Tokyo to clarify the situation.
subfiles.title: Letter from Roswell H. Whitman to P. A. Menon regarding the availability of quinine in Japan

subfiles.about: The Department of State notifies the Indian Embassy that Japanese quinine stocks are classified as looted property and cannot be exported under Allied policy.
subfiles.from: Edwin M. Martin (Chief, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs, Department of State)
subfiles.summary: Edwin M. Martin follows up on Whitman's January 23 letter after receiving a response from SCAP headquarters in Tokyo. Martin informs P. A. Menon that the Supreme Commander determined that the quinine stocks on hand constitute looted property and are therefore unavailable for export under Far Eastern Commission policy FEC 011/12 on Restitution of Looted Property. Martin concludes by expressing regret that he must deliver an unfavorable decision after the Indian government waited so long for a reply.
subfiles.title: Letter from Edwin M. Martin to P. A. Menon regarding restitution of looted quinine stocks
